title: Superpower Glass machine-learning emotion feedback on Google Glass improves socialization scores in children with autism (Stanford cohorts)
summary: Stanford's Superpower Glass cut SRS-2 scores 7.38 points in 14 children and raised Vineland socialization 4.58 points in a 71-child RCT.
account: Superpower Glass, developed at Stanford University, runs a machine-learning facial-expression classifier on Google Glass. It shows a child which emotion a facing person is displaying. An at-home feasibility study had intake between July and October 2016 (day not given, so 1 July is used). In it, 14 children with autism completed the protocol. Total SRS-2 scores fell an average of 7.38 points and 12 of 14 families reported more eye contact (npj Digital Medicine, 2018). A randomized trial enrolled 71 children aged 6 to 12 from 1 November 2016 to 11 April 2018. Those adding the device to applied behavioral analysis therapy gained 4.58 points more on the Vineland socialization subscale than controls (P = .005). Three other primary measures did not reach significance (JAMA Pediatrics, 2019). Results are cohort-level.
purpose: Teach emotion recognition and facial engagement to children with autism through real-time wearable feedback
system: Superpower Glass: Google Glass with a real-time machine-learning facial emotion classifier and companion smartphone app
developer: Stanford University (Wall lab, Division of Systems Medicine and Department of Computer Science)
deployer: Participating families at home under the Stanford studies
segment: Children with autism spectrum disorder aged 6-12
taxonomy_note: The measured gain is social-skills learning in children with autism, a therapeutic outcome that no type names exactly.

ratings.reason: The gains are group means (SRS-2 and Vineland), with no individually attributed outcome.
Trial evidence of efficacy comparable to standard care, not a measured societal change.

ai_role.statement: The emotion classifier, trained on public facial-expression databases and tuned for home conditions, generates the real-time cues the intervention relies on. The Guess the Emotion game within the package does not use the classifier. So part of the effect may come from structured family interaction rather than the AI.

headline: Superpower Glass raises Vineland socialization by 4.58 points
metric: gained 4.58 points more on the Vineland socialization subscale than controls (P = .005)

comparator.against: applied behavioral analysis therapy alone (treatment as usual)
comparator.quote: Children receiving the intervention showed significant improvements on the Vineland Adaptive Behaviors Scale socialization subscale compared with treatment as usual controls (mean [SD] treatment impact, 4.58 [1.62]; P = .005).

later.note: The feasibility cohort was followed by a 71-child randomized clinical trial at Stanford that found a socialization gain comparable with standard-of-care therapy.
later.quote: The observed 4.58-point average gain on the Vineland Adaptive Behaviors Scale socialization subscale is comparable with gains observed with standard of care therapy.
